statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-3783: when an HTTP(S) transfer that uses an OAuth2 bearer token follows a redirect to a second host that has an entry (a machine or default line) in the .netrc file in use, curl can pass the bearer token set for the first host on to the second one (https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-3783.html). It affects curl 7.33.0 to 8.18.0 and was fixed in curl 8.19.0 by https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/e3d7401a32a46516c9e5ee877e613e62ed35bddc, which sends the bearer token only when authentication is allowed to that host. The DHI curl packages for Alpine 3.23 are builds of curl 8.17.0-r1, 8.18.0-r0 (in both the main and the security repository), 8.19.0-r0, 8.20.0-r0, 8.20.0-r1, 8.21.0-r0, 8.22.0-r0, 8.23.0-r0 and 8.23.0-r1, and the version string in each build's libcurl matches its package version. The builds before 8.19.0-r0 are curl 8.17.0 and 8.18.0 without the fix (the security-repository 8.18.0-r0 build has the same machine code in the HTTP module of its static libcurl.a as the main-repository 8.18.0-r0 build, on x86_64 and aarch64), so 8.19.0-r0, the first build of curl 8.19.0, is the first fixed build.

CVE-2026-3783: when an HTTP(S) transfer that uses an OAuth2 bearer token follows a redirect to a second host that has an entry (a machine or default line) in the .netrc file in use, curl can pass the bearer token set for the first host on to the second one (https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-3783.html). It affects curl 7.33.0 to 8.18.0 and was fixed in curl 8.19.0 by https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/e3d7401a32a46516c9e5ee877e613e62ed35bddc, which sends the bearer token only when authentication is allowed to that host. Debian backported the fix to trixie in 8.14.1-2+deb13u4 (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-3783). The DHI curl packages for Debian 13 are rebuilds of Debian's trixie curl 8.14.1-2; the DHI Debian repository publishes three of them (the rebuild of 8.14.1-2+deb13u5 and two rebuilds of 8.14.1-2+deb13u7) for amd64 and arm64. Every published build is based on 8.14.1-2+deb13u5 or later, and the Debian changelog each one ships records the fix under 8.14.1-2+deb13u4, so the lowest published build, the rebuild of 8.14.1-2+deb13u5, is the fixed version used here. Earlier rebuilds of 8.14.1-2+deb13u3 and before, which this request also matches, are no longer published; they are based on Debian releases from before the fix and sort below the fixed version.
